official.deadline_note: Regular Action and Transfer aid applications are due 15 February (2027-02-15); continuing students reapply by 15 February for the following academic year. Deadlines are the same for domestic and international students. Late applications carry no penalty but must be received before the end of the academic year (mid-May for most students, mid-December for those attending only in the fall) to receive aid in that year.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 admissions cycle (entry fall 2027): Early Action application due 1 November 2026 with aid documents due 30 November 2026; Regular Action application due 4 January 2027 with aid documents due 15 February 2027. Offers are released mid-January (EA) and mid-March (RA).
official.status_note: MIT Admissions states the first-year application is open in the MIT application portal; financial aid applications are managed separately through the CSS Profile and College Board IDOC and are due with each admissions round.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Beginning with the 2025-2026 academic year, students from families with an annual income under $200,000 typically attend MIT tuition-free, meaning grant and scholarship aid will cover at least the cost of MIT's tuition ($66,720 for 2026-2027). More broadly, the MIT Scholarship makes up the difference between the cost of attendance and your family financial responsibility.
benefits: MIT Scholarship: a grant from MIT's endowment and general funds, given solely on the basis of need, that makes up the difference between the cost of attendance and your family financial responsibility; it does not need to be repaid.
First Year Grant of $2,000 for highest-need first-year students, divided equally between the fall and spring semesters, to help with extra expenses that come with the transition to college.

Health Insurance Grant covering the cost of the MIT Student Health Insurance Plan (MIT SHIP) for highest-need undergraduates who do not otherwise have adequate health insurance to meet the waiver requirements.
Students from families with an annual income under $200,000 typically attend MIT tuition-free, beginning with the 2025-2026 academic year.
For the 50% of American families with income below $100,000, parents can expect to pay nothing at all toward the full cost of attendance.
eligibility: You are classified as 'international' for financial aid purposes if you are not eligible for federal student financial aid as determined by FAFSA; U.S. citizens and permanent residents follow the domestic process, regardless of your place of residency.

International students are considered for aid using the same process MIT uses for all applicants; MIT commits to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need for international students, just as for domestic students.
MIT is need-blind and full-need for all of its undergraduate students, domestic and international; most MIT students receive need-based aid.
All students who apply for financial aid and fill out the CSS Profile are automatically considered for an MIT Scholarship.
The first-year application is intended for students who have concluded their secondary education and wish to pursue a bachelor's degree as a full-time university student.
requirements: Submit the CSS Profile designating MIT (CSS Code 3514) and answer all supplemental questions specific to MIT.
Submit parental tax returns or income documentation to the College Board's Institutional Documentation Service (IDOC) for processing; documents sent directly to MIT cannot be accepted.
Allow up to two weeks for tax returns to be received by MIT, and about 10 business days for documents to appear in the MIT Online Financial Aid System.
If your parents are separated or divorced, each parent must complete their own CSS Profile application and provide their own income documentation.
If awarded an MIT Scholarship, fill out an annual Student Information Review Form between May 1 and July 1 so MIT can match you with the right scholarship fund.
documents: CSS Profile (College Board) designating MIT, CSS Code 3514, with all MIT supplemental questions answered.
Parents' income tax returns or wage statements from two years ago, plus any other records of money earned.
For parents living outside the U.S., the tax return from that country with a translation to English if applicable (professional translation is not required).
Current bank account balances, records of investments, and records of untaxed income.
Noncustodial parent documentation if applicable; a waiver of noncustodial parent information may be requested where extenuating circumstances prevent it from being provided.
selection_criteria: Awards are made solely on the basis of demonstrated financial need: the difference between the cost of attendance and what the family is reasonably expected to contribute.

Need analysis considers the number of people in the family, the number of children currently attending college as an undergraduate, country/state of primary residence, total parent income from all sources (taxable and untaxed), taxes paid, non-reimbursed medical expenses, private school tuition for younger siblings, and total assets.
Each financial aid application is read by two financial aid officers to help ensure consistency and impartiality across cases.
About 58% of MIT undergraduates receive MIT Scholarships.
coverage: Tuition ($66,720 in 2026-2027) and the student life fee ($420), within the difference between the cost of attendance and family financial responsibility.

Housing ($14,090), food ($8,104), books, course materials, supplies and equipment ($930), and personal expenses ($2,496) within the 2026-2027 cost of attendance of $92,760 used to calculate the MIT Scholarship.
A travel allowance estimated based on where you live, added to the cost of attendance used to calculate need (not included in the published $92,760 total because it is specific to your address).
The MIT Student Health Insurance Plan (MIT SHIP) for highest-need undergraduates through the Health Insurance Grant.
application_method: Submit the CSS Profile online through the College Board, designating MIT with CSS Code 3514 and answering all MIT supplemental questions.
Submit parental tax returns or income documentation to the College Board's Institutional Documentation Service (IDOC).
Track financial aid documents in the MIT Application Portal ('Track Financial Aid Documents'), then view offers in the MIT Online Financial Aid System after enrollment.
official.application_route: Apply for undergraduate admission in the MIT application portal, then submit the CSS Profile (CSS Code 3514) plus parental income documents via College Board IDOC by the round deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time (the first-year application is for students who wish to pursue a bachelor's degree as a full-time university student).
official.citizenship_residency: Open to U.S. citizens, permanent residents and applicants of any nationality; for aid purposes 'international' means not eligible for federal student financial aid under FAFSA rules, regardless of place of residency.
official.international_eligibility: Yes: international students are considered for aid using the same process as all other applicants, and MIT commits to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need for international students.
official.duration: Aid is awarded for each academic year of the undergraduate degree and reviewed annually; continuing students reapply by 15 February for the following academic year.
official.description: MIT is need-blind and full-need for all undergraduates, domestic and international: the MIT Scholarship is a grant from MIT's endowment and general funds, awarded solely on the basis of demonstrated need, that makes up the difference between the cost of attendance and your family financial responsibility. About 58% of undergraduates receive an MIT Scholarship; the median MIT Scholarship was $73,666 for 2025-2026.
official.program_type: Need-blind, full-need institutional grant aid (MIT Scholarship) for undergraduate students, including international students, at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

not_confirmed: No fixed award amount is published; awards vary with each family's finances, so the $73,666 figure is the published median for 2025-2026 rather than a guaranteed amount.
Student Financial Services publishes no English-language requirement for the aid itself; the English proficiency exam guidance is published separately by MIT Admissions.
MIT publishes the aid deadlines as month and day only; the calendar years were mapped from MIT Admissions' currently open 2026-2027 application cycle.
verification.notes: Every figure, deadline and eligibility rule was read directly from MIT Student Financial Services (sfs.mit.edu) pages plus MIT Admissions' 2026-2027 cycle pages; no aggregator or third-party source was used.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate scholarship form: you are considered for an MIT Scholarship automatically the moment you submit the CSS Profile alongside your MIT undergraduate application. The real work is documenting your family's finances in detail through the College Board's IDOC service, and the size of the award is simply MIT's cost of attendance minus what your family is expected to pay. Families earning under $200,000 can realistically expect tuition to be fully covered, and under $100,000 MIT expects no parent contribution at all, though students are still expected to contribute from summer savings and term-time work. Start IDOC early, because documents can take up to two weeks to reach MIT and ten business days to show up in the portal.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International and domestic undergraduates admitted to or targeting MIT whose families cannot meet MIT's $92,760 cost of attendance and who can produce translated parental tax and income documentation.
application_readiness_checklist: Designate MIT (CSS Code 3514) in the CSS Profile and complete every MIT supplemental question; unanswered supplements stall the file.

Collect prior-prior-year parental tax returns or wage statements for both parents now; for parents outside the U.S., obtain that country's tax return plus an English translation (family members can translate).
Upload everything to College Board IDOC, never to MIT directly, and allow two weeks for delivery plus ten business days for portal processing.
If your parents are separated or divorced, have each parent complete their own CSS Profile and supply their own income documentation.

Diary your round deadline: 30 November for Early Action, 15 February for Regular Action and Transfer; late applications are accepted with no penalty but must arrive before mid-May to count for that academic year.
After enrolling, submit the annual Student Information Review Form between 1 May and 1 July so the scholarship can be matched to the right fund.
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete IDOC packets: one parent's missing tax return, bank statement or untaxed-income record freezes the award until it arrives.
Noncustodial parent information withheld without requesting the waiver MIT offers for extenuating circumstances.
Continuing students who miss the 15 February reapplication deadline and lose need-based aid for the following year.
Aid documents submitted after the academic year ends (mid-May, or mid-December for fall-only attendees), which cannot be considered for aid in that year.
Untranslated or unexplained foreign income documents, which force guesswork about family finances and can drag out review.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: For a student with no expected family contribution nothing is left uncovered; the median net price actually paid by an MIT Scholarship recipient was $11,432 in 2025-2026. Expect to fund a student contribution from summer savings and term-time work (the median family contribution before student term-time work was $8,967), and families above $200,000 income faced a median net price of $49,083, so higher-income families should plan for substantial self-funding.
document_audit: Documents go to College Board IDOC only; anything sent to sfs@mit.edu or MIT directly is not accepted.
Income must be from two years ago (prior-prior year), not last year's return.
English translations of foreign tax documents are required but professional translation is not; family members can translate.
Bank balances, investments and untaxed income are requested in addition to tax returns.
Both parents' documentation is required when parents are separated or divorced, and each files their own CSS Profile.
alerts: The aid application runs separately from the admission application: apply for admission by 1 November (EA) or 4 January (RA), but submit CSS Profile and IDOC documents by 30 November or 15 February respectively.

MIT requires the SAT or ACT (taken before 30 November for EA, before 31 December for RA) and strongly recommends an English proficiency exam for non-native speakers who have used English fewer than five years (IELTS minimum 7, TOEFL minimum 90, Duolingo minimum 120, PTE minimum 65, Cambridge minimum 185); RA English scores are accepted through the January test dates.
Only one application per entry year is allowed: a student denied Early Action cannot apply Regular Action that year.
Even with a $0 parent contribution (families under $100,000 income), students are still expected to contribute via summer savings and term-time work.
Awardees may occasionally be asked to write to their donor so they can connect with an MIT alum over shared interests and affinities.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application in the MIT portal first, then CSS Profile (MIT code 3514) plus IDOC documents by the round deadline; offers arrive by email from sfs@mit.edu and in the Application Portal in mid-January (EA) or mid-March (RA), then live in the Online Financial Aid System after enrollment.
